group.title: Family and relationships
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A boy or man who is the son of your stepmother or stepfather.
examples: My {stepbrother} moved in when our parents got married.
wrong: My stepbrother is my real brother; we have the same mother and father.

words.meaning: A girl or woman who is the daughter of your stepmother or stepfather.
examples: My {stepsister} and I share a bedroom now.
wrong: My stepsister is my aunt, my father’s sister.

words.meaning: A brother who has only one of the same parents as you.
examples: My {half-brother} has the same dad as me but a different mom.
wrong: My half-brother and I have the same mother and the same father.

words.meaning: The mother of your grandmother or grandfather.
examples: My {great-grandmother} is ninety-five years old.
wrong: My great-grandmother is younger than my mother.

words.meaning: No longer married because the marriage ended by law.
examples: Her parents are {divorced}, so she has two homes.
wrong: They are divorced and still live together as husband and wife.

words.meaning: A man whose wife has died.
examples: He became a {widower} when his wife died last year.
wrong: He is a widower, and his wife is waiting for him at home.

words.meaning: To go out with someone you like to see if you want a romantic relationship.
examples: They {went on a date} to the movies on Saturday.
wrong: We went on a date, but we never met or spoke that day.

words.meaning: A party where relatives from many places meet after a long time apart.
examples: All my cousins came to the {family reunion} last summer.
wrong: At the family reunion, no relatives came at all.

words.meaning: To start to love someone in a romantic way.
examples: They {fell in love} at university.
wrong: They fell in love, so they never wanted to see each other again.

words.meaning: To touch someone with your lips to show love or say hello.
examples: She {kissed} her baby goodnight.
wrong: He kissed his mother on the cheek with his elbow.

words.meaning: The relationship between two people who are husband and wife.
examples: Their {marriage} has lasted fifty years.
wrong: A marriage is a short chat between two strangers on a bus.

words.meaning: The woman who is married to your father but is not your mother.
examples: My {stepmother} married my dad when I was six.
wrong: My stepmother is the woman who gave birth to me.

words.meaning: The man who is married to your mother but is not your father.
examples: My {stepfather} drives me to school every day.
wrong: My stepfather is my real dad, who was there when I was born.

words.meaning: To take another person’s child into your family and raise it as your own.
examples: They {adopted} a baby girl from another country.
wrong: They adopted a son, so they had no children in their family.

words.meaning: The mother of your husband or wife.
examples: My {mother-in-law} visits us every Sunday.
wrong: My mother-in-law is my own mother’s sister.

words.meaning: The father of your husband or wife.
examples: Her {father-in-law} gave a speech at the wedding.
wrong: My father-in-law is my wife’s brother.

words.meaning: A brother or sister.
examples: I have two {siblings}, a brother and a sister.
wrong: My sibling is my grandfather.

words.meaning: A holiday that two people take just after their wedding.
examples: They went to Italy for their {honeymoon}.
wrong: They went on their honeymoon ten years before they met.

words.meaning: The man who is getting married at a wedding.
examples: The {groom} waited nervously for his bride.
wrong: The groom is the woman in the white wedding dress.

words.meaning: A friend in another place who you write letters or messages to.
examples: My {pen pal} in Brazil sends me a letter every month.
wrong: My pen pal lives next door, and we never write to each other.

words.meaning: To become husband and wife in a ceremony.
examples: They {got married} on the beach last summer.
wrong: They got married, so now they are not husband and wife.

words.meaning: A friend you know very well and like a lot.
examples: Anna is a {close friend}, so I tell her everything.
wrong: He is a close friend, but I have never spoken to him.

words.meaning: A short or funny name that friends or family call you.
examples: His {nickname} is Bear because he is very big.
wrong: A nickname is the official name in your passport.

words.meaning: Your family name, which usually comes last.
examples: Her first name is Maria and her {surname} is Lopez.
wrong: My surname is the first name my friends call me.

words.meaning: To come together with someone, usually as planned.
examples: Let’s {meet up} for coffee after work.
wrong: We met up, so we never saw each other that day.

words.meaning: Used to show that two or more people do the same thing to one another.
examples: The two sisters help {each other} with homework.
wrong: Tom and Sue love each other, but Sue does not love Tom.

words.meaning: Oldest of the children in a family.
examples: Their {eldest} son is at university now.
wrong: Their eldest daughter is the baby, born last month after the others.

words.meaning: A woman whose husband has died.
examples: She became a {widow} when her husband died last year.
wrong: She is a widow, and her husband is cooking dinner.

words.meaning: Part of the same family.
examples: Are you two {related}? You look alike.
wrong: We are related, but we are not in the same family at all.

words.meaning: To feel that someone or something is important to you.
examples: I really {care about} my friends.
wrong: She cares about her brother, so she never thinks about him.

words.meaning: A child who has an older and a younger brother or sister.
examples: As the {middle child}, I have one older sister and one younger brother.
wrong: She is the middle child because she has no brothers or sisters.

words.meaning: Without other people.
examples: He lives {alone} in a small apartment.
wrong: She lives alone with her parents and three brothers.

words.meaning: To give birth to a child and become a parent.
examples: My sister is going to {have a baby} in May.
wrong: They had a baby, so there were no children in the family.

words.meaning: A baby that was born only a few days or weeks ago.
examples: The {newborn} slept in her mother’s arms.
wrong: The newborn just celebrated his eightieth birthday.

words.meaning: An agreement between two people to get married.
examples: They announced their {engagement} at dinner.
wrong: Their engagement means they have decided never to marry.

words.meaning: A person you used to be married to or used to date.
examples: She is still friends with her {ex}.
wrong: My ex is the person I am dating right now.

words.meaning: A friend you have known since you were young.
examples: Sam is a {childhood friend}; we met when we were six.
wrong: She is my childhood friend; we met last week at work.

words.meaning: To meet in a group and spend time with each other.
examples: The whole family {gets together} at New Year.
wrong: We got together, so we all stayed at home alone.

words.meaning: To walk or sit with your hand in another person’s hand.
examples: The couple {held hands} as they walked in the park.
wrong: They held hands while standing on opposite sides of the room.

words.meaning: A young child who is just learning to walk.
examples: The {toddler} fell over and laughed.
wrong: The toddler drove his car to work.
